thread:
Ava: quick heads-up — replayer cohort run for last week's prod traces shows a small token mismatch during KV warmup. Dump attached below.
Ben: hmm, mismatch size?
Ava: ~0.3% of requests diverged on the first 32 tokens; full bit-compare fails for ~720 traces in the sample.
Carla: are you using anon hashing or full user ids? we need to keep request ordering for warmup to match KV cache state.
Ava: anonymization uses cohort-hash (sha1 -> bucket) to preserve cross-request affinity, but we applied random sampling after hashing which shuffled temporal order.
Ben: that'll change KV cache lineage. for apples-to-apples we should sample trace indices with a fixed RNG seed and then replay preserving original timestamp order.
Ava: agreed. current command we used: ```./replay --trace traces/2026-03-10.gz --anon cohort --sample 0.001 --seed random``` needs to be: ```./replay --trace traces/2026-03-10.gz --anon cohort --sample 0.001 --seed 42 --preserve-order```
Dev-bot: run 1951234567: finished canary. diffs summary: total_traces=720, token_mismatch_traces=216, avg_first32_token_diff_pct=0.28%, notes=divergences concentrate on multi-turn sessions.
Sam: also saw that a recent kernel selector change defaults to fused-attn for short sequences; the fused implementation returns slightly different floating rounding -> tiny divergences. that can cascade because KV keys change.
Carla: exactly — if kernel delta causes even 1-2 tokens diff early, subsequent KV keys diverge and the difference snowballs.
Ben: proposed plan: 1) rerun with deterministic sampling + preserve-order. 2) do two-level bitwise compare: logits (float tolerance) and tokenized output (exact). 3) pin kernel selector to legacy path for A/B. 4) add per-request kv_warmup fingerprints to replay artifacts.
Ava: starting rerun now with `--seed 42 --preserve-order`. i'm also submitting a tiny PR to add `--preserve-order` to the replayer CLI. adding a wrapper to emit `kv_warmup_state` per request.
Carla: also add a CI canary lane: 1k-trace deterministic run (seed=42), compare logits (L2 < 1e-6) and token equality. if token equality fails, fail the lane.
Sam: suggestion: dump KV fingerprints (sha256 per layer) after warmup N tokens and store as `kv_fingerprint`. that gives us quick equality checks without storing large state.
Ben: agree. format example: `kv_fingerprint: layer0:abc123 layer1:def456 ...` store in artifact bucket and attach to run.
Ava: devops: how expensive is storing these fingerprints for every trace? @Devops
Devops: will chime in — approximate: 2KB per trace * 1000 traces = ~2MB, negligible for artifact storage.
Ben: timeline: canary run on harness takes ~45m. let's run in parallel on a dedicated 4-GPU pool so results by EOD.
Carla: owners: Ava -> run deterministic canary + upload logs, Sam -> investigate kernel selector diff and produce microbench with fused vs legacy, Ben -> add kv fingerprinting to replayer and wire CI lane. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
Ava: ack. uploading logs to s3://redwood-replay/canary/1951234567/ and artifact `kv_fingerprints.json` when done.
Sam: small control: also test with batching heuristics disabled (batch_size=1 / continuous_batching off) to isolate batching side effects.
Ava: added `--batch-size 1 --continuous-batching off` to the canary script. will run both modes.
Dev-bot: new run queued on dedicated-4gpu (job id: 5902). will post diffs once complete.
Ben: one more note — for apples-to-apples kernel selection we should export the `KERNEL_HINT` used per invocation and pin it in the A/B. that makes the comparison deterministic.
Carla: good call. add `kernel_hint` to replay metadata.
Ava: doing that now. quick results coming in: first run (preserve-order + seed=42 + batch-size=1) reduced token_mismatch_traces from 216 -> 3. looks like sampling/order was the main issue.
Sam: nice. those 3 are likely kernel selector rounding diffs. i'll run microbench and revert the fused-attn selector for the canary A branch.
Ben: once Sam has microbench, we can decide to either accept fused kernel (if within tolerance) or adjust fallback thresholds.
Ava: created issue RW-4312 with links to canary artifacts and diff logs. attaching short playbook for reproducing locally: ```./replay --trace traces/2026-03-10.gz --anon cohort --seed 42 --preserve-order --dump-kv-fingerprint kv_out.json --batch-size 1```
Carla: thanks — looks good. marking `#replayer-cohort-determinism` and adding to next eng-runtime retro.
Ava: will update RW-4312 with final results after Sam's microbench. :thumbsup:
Ben: thanks everyone. small wins — deterministic sampling + preserve-order should be standard in future apples-to-apples perf runs.
